## Proof

By the spectral theorem for self-adjoint operators, $A$ admits a spectral measure $E_A$, a projection-valued measure supported on the spectrum $\sigma(A)\subseteq\mathbb{R}$. The Borel (and in particular $C^\infty$) functional calculus defines
$$f(A) \;=\; \int_{\sigma(A)} f(\lambda)\,dE_A(\lambda),$$
understood as an operator on the Hilbert space, with the integral converging in the strong operator topology (and, since $f$ is bounded here, in the operator norm).

The hypothesis is
$$\operatorname{supp}(f)\cap\sigma(A)=\varnothing.$$

Since $E_A$ is supported on $\sigma(A)$, the integral over $\sigma(A)$ of any function equals the integral of that function restricted to $\sigma(A)$. On $\sigma(A)$, the hypothesis $\operatorname{supp}(f)\cap\sigma(A)=\varnothing$ means that every point of $\sigma(A)$ lies outside $\operatorname{supp}(f)$, i.e., $f$ vanishes on an open neighborhood of every point of $\sigma(A)$. Hence
$$f\big|_{\sigma(A)}\equiv 0.$$

Therefore
$$f(A)=\int_{\sigma(A)}f(\lambda)\,dE_A(\lambda)=\int_{\sigma(A)}0\,dE_A(\lambda)=0.$$

Concretely, for every vector $\xi$ in the Hilbert space,
$$\langle \xi, f(A)\xi\rangle=\int_{\sigma(A)}f(\lambda)\,d\langle \xi,E_A(\lambda)\xi\rangle=\int_{\sigma(A)}0\,d\mu_\xi(\lambda)=0,$$
where $\mu_\xi$ is the finite positive Borel measure $\mu_\xi(\cdot)=\langle\xi,E_A(\cdot)\xi\rangle$. Since this holds for all $\xi$, the positive operator $f(A)^*f(A)$ vanishes (applying the same argument to $|f|^2$, which also has support disjoint from $\sigma(A)$), so $f(A)=0$.

### PROOF COMPLETE
